children.translated_text: Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Thus have I heard: At one time the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling among the <s>Śākyas</s>, at <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> grove.

children.translated_text: protective spell (<s>vidyā</s>) named <s>Mekhalā</s>. Let the hosts of <s>devas</s> (gods), hosts of <s>nāgas</s> (serpents), hosts of <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons) hear me,
hosts of <s>asuras</s>, hosts of <s>garuḍas</s>, hosts of <s>gandharvas</s>, hosts of <s>kinnaras</s>,

children.text: cagaṇā kuṃbhāṇḍagaṇā pūtanagaṇā grahagaṇā nakṣatragaṇā aṣṭāviṃsati mahāyakṣasenāpati / catvāro mahārājānaḥ kṛmayo vītarāgaḥ himavaṃtanivāsino daśa dik* ye bhūtāḥ prativasaṃti rākṣasīgaṇāḥ pākiḍi / laṃbodari / kīṭakarṇa / sumanā ca / mahāratiḥ mātṛgaṇāś ca ye samudrakalpasya rakṣakaḥ purasmiṃ diśābhāge hari nāma rākṣasī : dakṣaṇasmiṃ diśābhāge goṇāsi nāma rākṣasī paścimasmiṃ diśābhāge kesari nāma rākṣasī / uttarasmiṃ diśābhāge mahācūḍā nāma rākṣasī ity etā rākṣasī ghori ekaikaḥ ṣaṣṭikoṭiparivṛtaḥ te rāhulasya kumārasya nityaṃ rakṣaṃ mekhalāvidyāyāḥ rakṣa rakṣa mama gornikṣiṇasya rakṣaṃ kurvatu / niveditāyāḥ tadyathā ghane ghane ghane ghane / ghaphu ghanapati / ghume ghume / (
children.translated_text: <s>piśācas</s>, hosts of <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, hosts of <s>pūtanas</s>, hosts of <s>grahas</s> (seizers), hosts of <s>nakṣatras</s> (constellations), the twenty-eight great <s>yakṣa</s> generals, the four great kings, worms, <s>Vītarāga</s>, dwellers of the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayas), whatever beings dwell in the ten directions, hosts of <s>rākṣasīs</s> — <s>Pākiḍi</s>, <s>Laṃbodarī</s>, <s>Kīṭakarṇā</s>, <s>Sumanā</s>, and <s>Mahārati</s>, and the hosts of mothers (<s>mātṛgaṇa</s>) who are protectors of the ocean-age. In the eastern direction is the <s>rākṣasī</s> named <s>Hari</s>; in the southern direction is the <s>rākṣasī</s> named <s>Goṇāsī</s>; in the western direction is the <s>rākṣasī</s> named <s>Kesarī</s>; in the northern direction is the <s>rākṣasī</s> named <s>Mahācūḍā</s>. These fearsome <s>rākṣasīs</s>, each surrounded by sixty <s>koṭis</s> (millions) — let them constantly protect the prince <s>Rāhula</s>! By the power of the <s>Mekhalā</s> spell, protect, protect! Perform protection for my child! As it has been announced: <s>tadyathā</s> — ghane ghane ghane ghane / ghaphu ghanapati / ghume ghume /

children.translated_text: ghume / ghume ghume ghume ghumapati / ghare ghare ghare ghare ghare / gharipaṭi harāpiṭi / śārāpati dhanāpati / surapati / ahiṅse ahiṃsapati / mamati / amati / sumati / bahupati hala hala hala / hala hala / hala halaṃ halapa : hili hili hili hili hili hili / hili / hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu / tili tili tili tili tili tili tili // ṣiṭi ṭape ṭaṭṛpe / olaṃbe mavisāre / haha hihi huhu / samatasare / asamaṃtacare palikhasare / acarte / samatacarte ghane mekhale. This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is that <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Mekhalā</s>, the universal protective talisman (<s>samantapratisarā</s>), which is never obstructed — not by <s>vidyādharas</s> (spell-bearers), not by <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits), not by <s>vetāḍas</s> (vampires), not by the greatly powerful, the supernaturally endowed, the greatly vigorous. This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Mekhalā</s> spell spoken by the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> for the benefit and happiness of beings, for the sake of protection and

children.translated_text: child! I perform protection within a circumference of twelve <s>yojanas</s>. I perform guarding, sheltering, shielding, pacification, and well-being. I perform the warding off of blows. I perform the warding off of weapons. I perform the neutralization of poison. I perform the repelling of enemies. I perform the binding of boundaries. I perform the binding of the cord (<s>sūtra</s>). I ward off all evils. Let no humans or non-humans, no wicked ones harm [him]! <s>svāhā</s>! || As the ritual practice: having paid homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> and offered flowers and incense, the cord should be made. Rubbing, anointing, and wiping should be performed. May there be the warding off of all <s>grahas</s> (malignant seizures),

body.translated_text: At that time, the prince <s>Rāhula</s>, lying on his bed, was frightened by a certain <s>rākṣasī</s> (demoness). Then, after the passing of that night, the prince <s>Rāhula</s>, surrounded and attended by many young boys, went forth from <s>Kapilavastu</s> and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and stood weeping before the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Learn, <s>Ānanda</s>, for the protection of the prince <s>Rāhula</s>, I will

children.text: śruṇitvāna / kaṃpitā sarva medini bhūtasaṃghāḥ pracalitā devasaṃghāḥ samāgatāḥ nāgarājāḥ samāgatāḥ bhūtarājāḥ samāgataḥ bhagava maitrakaṃ : brahmendrāś ca samāgataḥ maheśvaraś ca kumārāś cāpy ubhau samāgatau ye kecit kīrtitā bhūtā mekhalāya samāgata : atha maitreyo bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ bhagavantam etad avocat* aham asmiṃ bhagavan rāhulasya kumārasya rakṣāṃ dāsyāmi / paritraṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śānti svastyayanaṃ daṇ
children.translated_text: Having heard [this], the entire earth trembled, the hosts of beings were shaken, the assemblies of gods arrived, the <s>Nāga</s> kings arrived, the kings of spirits arrived. The <s>Bhagavān</s> [of] <s>Maitreya</s>[-kindness]: <s>Brahma</s>, <s>Indra</s> and others arrived, <s>Maheśvara</s> and <s>Kumāra</s> — both arrived, and whatever beings have been mentioned came together for the <s>Mekhalā</s> [rite]. Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Maitreya</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "I, <s>Bhagavān</s>, shall give protection (<s>rakṣā</s>) to prince <s>Rāhula</s> — shelter, safeguarding, guardianship, peace (<s>śānti</s>), well-being (<s>svastyayana</s>), the removal of the rod (<s>daṇḍa</s>),"
"the neutralization of poison, the warding off of enemies, the binding of the boundary (<s>sīmābandha</s>),"

children.text: ṃ sūtrakabandhaṃ mekhalāvidyāyāḥ parivārāḥ tadyathā acaṭanī caṭanī / .. .. .. .. .ī culu culu / ūrdhvadaṇḍe adhardaṇḍe samaṃtadaṇḍe / nimimune / śānti /
children.translated_text: "the binding of the thread (<s>sūtraka</s>). [These are] the retinue [mantras] of the <s>Mekhalā Vidyā</s> (Girdle Spell), namely: <s>acaṭanī caṭanī</s> ... <s>culu culu / ūrdhvadaṇḍe adhardaṇḍe samantadaṇḍe / nimimune / śānti</s>."
